title: An Automated Web-GIS and MATLAB Pipeline for Multi-Scale Cartographic Complexity Analysis and Coastal Feature Extraction
content: Quantifying coastal spatial complexity across continuous display scales in digital mapping architectures is traditionally constrained by static raster resolution boundaries, quantization errors, and manual operator bias. Furthermore, dynamic web-mapping services deploy scale-dependent cartographic generalization, causing displayed geometries to reflect geospatial database complexity rather than static physical boundaries. To address these challenges, this study presents an automated, hybrid Web-GIS and MATLAB geospatial processing pipeline that integrates commercial web-mapping API vector-rendering engines with digital image processing to facilitate continuous multi-scale cartographic complexity (Db) benchmarking and feature extraction. By maintaining a constant physical-scale measuring grid—calibrated via a dimensionless coordinate-ratio parameter—over programmatically scaled vector cartography, the pipeline leverages sub-pixel geometric precision to achieve seamless multi-scale coastal feature extraction. The framework incorporates connected-component labeling (CCL) noise filtration, Otsu thresholding, Canny edge detection, Gecko-engine tile rendering to eliminate WebKit-induced stitching grid artifacts, and latitudinal scale-distortion compensation for Web Mercator projections. Deployed across 16 global geospatial databases, the pipeline demonstrates robust spatial benchmarking capabilities: along Norway's glaciated coastline (Db=1.4395), it effectively captures a scale-dependent, biphasic "fjord-to-fjard" morphometric transition, resolving spatial thresholds corresponding to meso-scale glacial valley morphometry. Global database benchmarking reveals clear structural distinctions in cartographic complexity, where active convergent boundaries exhibit elevated fractal complexity (e.g., Southeast Asia, Db=1.4578) compared to transform-suppressed margins (e.g., US West Coast, Db=1.0460). Additionally, a macro-scale cartographic low-pass filter (>0.8 km, Zoom 2–7) effectively attenuates high-frequency cartographic noise and anthropogenic structural inflation (e.g., 56.29% artificial coastlines in Taiwan). This open-source workflow provides a robust, reproducible Web-GIS framework for dynamic spatial database benchmarking, digital cartographic analysis, and automated coastal feature extraction.
